messages.subject: Re: trouble importing genalex
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

Thank you for your email and thank you for supplying the necessary diagnostic information. I believe you've discovered an edge case. I have tried it on some random data using the same entries and have run into an error as well (although not the same error). I will investigate this when I get in next week. Since you have one locus, I would suggest removing the first two rows of your spreadsheet and collapsing the last two columns into a single column (separating the alleles with "/") and importing that using read.table and then using df2genind like so:

my_df <- read.table("myData.csv", sep = ",", header = TRUE)
my_data <- df2genind(my_df[-c(1, 2), , drop = FALSE], ind.names = my_df$ind, pop.names = my_df$pop, ploidy = TRUE, sep = "/")

Additionally:

> [1] "/Users/nickwong/Library/R/3.1/library/poppr/files/test.csv"
>

This is from your output. You should not be saving files in your R library. This is a space only for packages. The example using getfile was simply an example using files that I could ship with poppr.

> > myData<-read.genalex(x$files, ploidy = 2, geo = FALSE, region = FALSE)
> Error in if (any(gena.mat == "0") & ploidy < 3) { :
>   missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
> > traceback()
> 1: read.genalex(x$files, ploidy = 2, geo = FALSE, region = FALSE)
>

This error is telling me that there was a missing value in your data. You might have had extra rows or columns that didn't appear to have data in them; however given the error I got, the problem might go deeper.

Again, I will be investigating this further and will have it fixed in the next release.

Cheers,
Zhian

The issue should be fixed.
To fix it without re-installing poppr from source: https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905 (Note: if you choose this route, you must do this every time you restart R)

Link to the issue: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/58

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: nei distance using populations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zhian

I am using poppr v. 2.0.2.

I'd like to generate a tree based on Nei's genetic distances.

I can do this as per the manual on all individuals.

aboot(a,cutoff = 70, tree="nj",quiet = TRUE, sample = 1000, distance = nei.dist)

But I want to do this between populations, I tried using the "strata" option here but it didn't work.

aboot(a,strata = ~METAPOP2, cutoff = 70, tree="nj",quiet = TRUE, sample = 1000, distance = nei.dist)

Is there a way to do this from within poppr?

Thanks!

Monique

messages.subject: Re: nei distance using populations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Monique

To generate a tree among populations, simply convert your genind to a genpop object. You can find an example in the "Population Structure" chapter in our Population Genetics in R manual:

http://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/Pop_Structure.html#genetic-distance

# Setup
library("poppr")
library("magrittr") # for the %>% "pipe" operator
data("microbov")
strata(microbov)     <- data.frame(other(microbov))
nameStrata(microbov) <- ~Country/Breed/Species

# Analysis
set.seed(999)
microbov %>%
  genind2genpop(pop = ~Country/Breed) %>%
  aboot(cutoff = 50, quiet = TRUE, sample = 1000, distance = nei.dist)

aboot doesn't have a strata argument specifically, but it's a good idea to have one as a signal to convert to a genpop object. I'll add it in the next version.

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject_clean: assigning names to mlgs in genclone object
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

First off, very happy with poppr -  it's making my data analysis a lot easier!

My question: I'm relatively new to R and poppr.  I want to use the mlg.table function barplots, but I'd like to change the mlg names on the x axis  from the default numbers to those I have in my database. How can I go about doing this?

If it's of any use, I included the MLG names as a stratum when i imported my dataset.

Thanks,

Jay

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jay,

You can use the mll.custom function to define your custom multilocus genotypes.

You can find a small example in the Multilocus Genotype Analysis vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/mlg.html#custom-custom

Hope that helps!

Zhian
